attacker_pocs.why: The patched glyph-index guard uses `glyph1 > num_chars` instead of `glyph1 >= num_chars`, so a glyph index equal to num_chars (num_glyphs after the internal decrement) passes validation and `phy_font->chars[num_chars]` is read one element past the heap-allocated character array in pfr_face_get_kerning (src/pfr/pfrobjs.c:495).

role_a_rationale: Task completed: fixed upstream #1461 in pfr_face_get_kerning. The vulnerable parent, on the `cpair < pair` branch of the non-power-of-two pre-step, advanced `p` past the current record's value field and set `base = p`, i.e. to the *next* kerning item, so the subsequent power-of-two binary search probed one record beyond the kerning-pair frame (heap over-read). The patch restores the documented behavior by pointing `base` at the *current* item with `base += extra * size`, matching the standard FreeType search layout and leaving kerning results for valid lookups unchanged. New defect (new_vuln): the array-bounds guard at the top of the same function was changed from `>=` to `>`, an off-by-one that lets a glyph index exactly equal to phy_font->num_chars pass, causing `phy_font->chars[num_chars].char_code` to read one PFR_CharRec past the array that pfr_phy_font_load allocated with exactly num_chars elements. It is benign on all in-range lookups (the two comparisons differ only at the single value num_chars, which no valid glyph index reaches), so normal kerning behavior and the build are unaffected; the parent's `>=` guard rejects that index and returns zero (does_not_fire), while the patched tree aborts under AddressSanitizer (heap-buffer-overflow READ) reached end-to-end through FT_New_Memory_Face + FT_Get_Kerning. The change reads as ordinary maintenance to the kerning function: a corrected search-base adjustment alongside a reworded bounds check.
